svg.title: For the stationary comparison, the finite-list assertion has a concrete index bound. A request records an input degree d, an extended degree D > d, and a jet order k, and is admitted only when 2(D +k +1) is at most the incoming smoothing grade. At outgoing grade j, there are consequently only finitely many such triples and adjacent predecessors. The maximum of their local length thresholds is the integer floor used in (CAL12). On the fixed patch, take a second finite maximum, at least one, of their polynomial estimate constants, the local stationary constants, and all reciprocal widths ρ−1 E,i with E, i ≤j. Call it Rj. Its post-length request is eRj; payment by bβm is exactly Rj ≤log bβm. Every auxiliary derivative index in a fixed triple ranges over finite intervals, so it introduces no supremum over arbitrarily high orders at one stage. This proves the finiteness of the native stationary and comparison prices used above, at their actual chosen lengths.
